title: A longer digital-protest backstory
summary: The Arab uprisings show that youth mobilization, public-space occupation and networked communication have a long history; the digital ecosystem evolves rather than being invented in 2025.

title: Sri Lanka's Aragalaya
summary: Economic collapse and anger at political leadership foreground the gap between forcing a leader out and rebuilding durable institutions.

title: Bangladesh: quota dispute becomes an uprising
summary: A public-service quota dispute expands into a national challenge to the ruling order. The UN later estimates as many as 1,400 deaths between 1 July and 15 August.

title: Kenya: Reject the Finance Bill
summary: The proposed taxes feed demonstrations. The bill is withdrawn, but rights and accountability questions continue.

title: Serbia: student blockades
summary: Students press for documents and accountability after a fatal station-canopy collapse. The prime minister resigns, but accountability is not finished.

title: Indonesia: allowances and police conduct
summary: Lawmakers' benefits symbolize privilege amid wider anger; subsequent rights reporting describes alleged excessive force.

title: Timor-Leste: cars and pensions
summary: Students protest a US$4.2m official-vehicle plan; parliament abandons the purchase and votes to abolish lifetime pensions.

title: Philippines: flood-control corruption
summary: Public anger over alleged ghost or defective projects moves from online scrutiny to large Manila demonstrations.

title: Nepal: platform ban accelerates a wider crisis
summary: A social-media ban becomes a visible trigger amid anger about corruption and nepotism. First-day deaths and broader totals cover different windows.

title: Madagascar and Morocco: service delivery becomes political
summary: Water, power, health and education failures become legitimacy tests. Outcomes diverge: a military-led transition in Madagascar, concessions and repression in Morocco.

title: Peru: pension reform in a broader crisis
summary: Youth-led protests amplify wider frustration, but the later presidential removal is not attributable to one cause.

title: Bulgaria: budget protest and resignation
summary: CIVICUS reports a budget withdrawal and government resignation amid mass protest; the exact role of youth should not be overstated.

title: Bangladesh: the ballot tests the uprising's legacy
summary: The BNP wins a large majority; the youth-linked party wins six seats. Reporting questions whether post-uprising reform lasts.

title: Indonesia: legal afterlife
summary: Four activists are acquitted, demonstrating how a protest's aftermath moves through courts and accountability.

title: India: voter-list revision becomes a flashpoint
summary: Reuters reports detentions during a dispute over voter-list revision. The administrative figures and allegations of partisan intent are distinct claims.

title: France and Albania: parallel student mobilizations
summary: Students protest school conditions and higher-education concerns. Evidence does not establish one global command linking these cases.
